rows.purpose: Open or resume a verified full-model session in the application's working environment.

requirements: X-01: Preserve canonical asset and proof-source bytes through default Windows checkouts and packaging, and verify their digests before enabling the model without changing its manifest identity.
Retain all 259,800 labelled slots and all 1,200 legal generators; presentation changes must never change mechanics or relabel pieces.
Resume saved work and preferences directly, and provide a clearly labelled fresh practice copy of the full model.
Replace MPUlt reflection, Managed DirectX preparation and the old compile cache with the selected 1.0 platform boundary; do not assume the 0.4 process split.
If a local engine process is owned, preserve authenticated health, graceful shutdown and parent-death recovery through EngineProcess.
rows.notes: Stage 2.2 proposal based on source inventories only; flows are provisional. This file makes no Windows/DirectX, input or performance claim, and delete/automate decisions require the owner's later signature.

rows.purpose: Establish that the displayed geometry, labels and move mapping belong to the complete authoritative model before interaction.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM supports safe F-SESSION and F-EXECUTE; charter sections 2 and 4 preserve model verification while replacing the MPUlt bridge.
requirements: Retain all 259,800 labelled slots and all 1,200 legal generators; presentation changes must never change mechanics or relabel pieces.
Verify geometry, model identity and source-to-destination generator mappings before enabling interaction; reject partial or mismatched models.
Synchronize committed labels, view context and revisions before accepting input, and make reconnect failure recoverable.
Put platform-specific renderer connection behind a narrow interface without requiring the retained assembly or its reflection names.

rows.purpose: Leave a session safely and recover its last durable work after interruption.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and solving-workflow section 4.2 require interruption and resume to preserve state and history; charter section 4 replaces the old window lifecycle.

Dispose rendering and owned resources safely, and preserve graceful owned-engine shutdown and parent-pipe recovery.

rows.purpose: Reclaim working space by revealing or dismissing supporting tools without losing their context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE needs efficient access to preparation tools; charter section 5 D5 and the owner's design decision section 6 require adaptable space with both principal views visible.
requirements: Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Global and Local must remain visible together, sharing one context and revision; opening an inspection must not create a third view.
Retain drafts and tool context across visibility and window-size changes; do not silently hide a required view to fit a panel.

rows.purpose: Reach the presentation settings that make geometry and projection comfortable to inspect.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-FIND need legible presentation; charter section 5 permits validated user tuning within the two theme families.
requirements: Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Expose validated view settings through the shared command layer and preferences, with fixed interaction and status meanings across themes.
Keep display tuning separate from model geometry, piece identity and the solver's fixed Grip frame.

rows.purpose: Allocate useful space between geometric work and supporting tools as the workspace size changes.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE is served by readable, adaptable work areas; charter section 5 D5 and anti-goal 11 require layout to survive resizing and DPI changes.
requirements: Global and Local must remain visible together, sharing one context and revision; opening an inspection must not create a third view.
Preserve the user's chosen allocation and tool context while maintaining legible geometry and reachable controls across resizing and DPI changes.
Provide a keyboard route for adjusting or restoring the working allocation without specifying 0.4 divider sizes.

rows.purpose: Tune geometric separation, camera projection and lighting for readable structure.

requirements: Retain all 259,800 labelled slots and all 1,200 legal generators; presentation changes must never change mechanics or relabel pieces.

Validate user tuning for legibility and the renderer gate in both theme families.

parts.purpose: Adjust camera perspective to compare the relevant places comfortably.

State the projection basis and units, validate its range, and keep the same interaction meaning across themes.

parts.purpose: Tune surface shading and highlights to make the structure readable.
parts.reason: F-FIND relies on legibility; charter section 5 A3 and the owner's design decision section 3 retain comfortable tuning within validated themes.

Each theme family's most expensive approved scene must meet the full-detail renderer gate; lighting changes cannot alter picking or mechanics.

rows.purpose: Learn the available actions, mathematical terms and safety guarantees in the current task.

Distinguish pending preview, accepted operation and stale display; no rejected or uncertain operation may look successfully committed.
Do not retain an instant-only runtime promise as a user option.

rows.purpose: Reveal or hide the structural framework to support the current inspection.

Reset only the declared camera and display parameters, preserving labels, journal, filters, drafts, target, buffers and protection.
Restoring a view must not silently change physical key meanings or the fixed Grip frame; any needed engine lookup runs asynchronously.

rows.purpose: Bring the focused canonical cell into geometric view.

Center on the exact cell in the shared Global/Local context without changing mechanics, target, buffers or an assigned Grip frame.

rows.purpose: Find the preparation, inspection and recovery tools relevant to the current work.

Organize surviving tools around the solver's current orbit, target, roles and revision; do not reproduce fixed tab indices or a second context.
Keep every surviving action reachable through the command palette and retain unfinished edits when focus changes.

rows.purpose: Save a named durable recovery point for the current work.

Capture exact labels, model identity, journal location and the declared workspace/view context coherently and durably.
Name the checkpoint and report its actual save outcome; failure must leave existing checkpoints and current work intact.
Checkpoint metadata must remain lightweight to enumerate without reading label blobs.

rows.purpose: Choose a canonical cell as the shared focus for structural work.

Use exact canonical cell IDs and one revision across both views; focus selection alone must not turn, assign a Grip or move the camera.

Queue or reject context changes coherently during a job, preventing an older focus response from replacing the latest selection.

rows.purpose: Make a recoverable local copy of the session journal.

Report completion and the recoverable artifact only after publication succeeds; preserve the source on failure.
Keep backup distinct from proof-log export, which may have format limits.

rows.purpose: Save a portable verified record of the selected session history and its legal evidence.

requirements: A-02: Validate export primitive and transaction budgets against the paired importer before writing; refuse an unimportable record and offer a session backup.

Export exact model identity, labelled state, chronological source-to-destination witnesses and the declared branch scope.
Publish atomically to the solver's chosen local destination, with a failed export leaving any prior file intact.
An export is not a certificate of a solve unless exact whole-model completion was verified.

rows.purpose: Choose the working orbit and understand its exact remaining work.
rows.reason: The correspondence joins orbit selection with residual reporting; F-TARGET and F-ENDGAME retain both under solving-workflow sections 2, 3.4 and 4.2.

Invalidate execution permission and resolve identities against current state when changing or resuming an orbit; never advance automatically.

rows.purpose: Save the session's verified legal history as a local log.

Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Preserve chronological legal witnesses, exact labels, model identity and provenance in the declared log format.

rows.purpose: Edit and apply a whole-piece work filter without changing the puzzle.

Keep unapplied filter edits distinct from active rules and preserve those edits through unrelated refreshes.
Evaluate filters as whole-piece predicates with separate visible and interactive scopes; filters must not remove mechanical labels or legal generators.
Protection conflicts and complete-operation effects must remain visible through filters, and reference-only buffers must remain noninteractive.

rows.purpose: Restore work from a verified legal log while retaining a recovery point for the current session.

requirements: Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Validate the complete bounded input, model identity, all legal witnesses and exact replay result before any database writes.
Import transactionally, retain current preferences and the recovery checkpoint, and leave current state unchanged after validation or publication failure.
A-02: Enforce documented paired log budgets and give a specific recovery option for an over-budget record.
Keep legacy-log reading behind an importer; full 0.4 session migration reads a locked database copy including WAL commits, without modifying the original or using immutable=1.
Require fresh confirmation of the inspected file digest and import scope; no retained-host launch is required for path B.

rows.purpose: Inspect the exact piece and sticker counts of an unapplied filter.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-CHECK need a safe filter preview; solving-workflow section 4.3 keeps a display query separate from mechanical state.
requirements: Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Evaluate draft predicates without applying them, using the same whole-piece semantics as actual application.
Return exact piece and slot counts with current state/filter context, reject obsolete replies, and show parsing or query failures as errors rather than zero matches.
Do not block the UI or discard unfinished filter edits while counting.

rows.purpose: Export recorded puzzle work to a chosen portable log file.

requirements: A-02: Validate export primitive and transaction budgets against the paired importer before writing; refuse an unimportable record and offer a session backup.
Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
State each output format's model, witness and replay guarantees; never imply that a lossy compatibility log is a full certificate.
Write the complete validated record atomically to a chosen local file and keep current session data intact.
The 1.0 format contract is settled at its freeze; the old MPUlt format choice does not imply retaining the MPUlt runtime or a reverse session-migration path.

rows.purpose: Prepare a useful work filter from the current orbit, piece or structural context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-FIND benefit from reusable filters; solving-workflow section 4.3 requires explicit work scope without changing mechanics.
requirements: Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Resolve preset parameters from the shared current context and explain whether they follow identities, positions or a live query.
Keep staging and applying a preset explicit and consistent; parameterized structural presets require a fresh count review before application.
Do not use presets to hide protection conflicts or operation collateral, and do not silently retarget a saved work set.

rows.purpose: Undo a committed operation exactly while keeping its journal branch recoverable.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE and F-SESSION require exact undo; solving-workflow section 4.2 and charter section 5 E4 preserve history through mistakes and interruption.
requirements: X-02: Keep checkpoint blob scans out of commit, undo and redo status refreshes; use lightweight metadata and check latency as automatic checkpoints accumulate.
Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Undo through the authoritative journal with exact labelled state and durable outcome; preserve alternate branches and invalidate pending execution permission.
Editor undo must remain separate from puzzle undo; a held committing key must not repeat.
Withdraw current achievements and pending celebrations on undo while preserving already unlocked explanations and user-saved macros.

rows.purpose: Redo an undone journal operation with exact state and a clear durable outcome.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE and F-SESSION need reversible history; solving-workflow section 4.2 and charter section 5 E4 require state and history to stay consistent.
requirements: X-02: Keep checkpoint blob scans out of commit, undo and redo status refreshes; use lightweight metadata and check latency as automatic checkpoints accumulate.
Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Redo from the declared journal branch and current context, retain exact labelled state and invalidate stale previews.
Distinguish a completed redo from a failed display refresh and prevent a held key or a refresh retry from repeating the operation.

rows.purpose: Keep target, buffer and operation references visible outside the interactive work filter.

Show fixed buffer positions and their changing occupants distinctly, using exact IDs and the shared encoding grammar.

Persist bindings in the session/workspace boundary and retain an invalid previous file for recovery instead of overwriting it with defaults.
Camera, filters, moving pieces and theme changes must not silently remap physical keys; show the active mapping and support explicit switching.
Keep all 1,200 generators reachable and every program operation available in the command palette; keys use soft disclosure without withholding functions.

rows.purpose: Include or exclude whole orbits from the interactive work display.

Compose explicit whole-piece orbit predicates with existing rules and preserve their declared styling semantics.
An empty work set must be reported as empty, never as completion; hidden orbits still participate in effects, protection and exact state.
Treat orbit visibility and protection as separate commands and facts, and keep required context references visible.

Never repeat a committing command from a held key; text editors and focused view controls own their normal navigation and edit keys.
Keep cancellation and necessary view access available during jobs without letting unrelated keys bypass busy or permission gates.
Replace the assisted-insertion shortcut with only surviving commands; explicit target, macro and execution choices remain the solver's actions.
Do not inherit the 0.4 key assignments; 1.0 mappings are set by the design track.

rows.purpose: Prepare a recorded legal scramble for deliberate practice or a new attempt.

Retain all 259,800 labelled slots and all 1,200 legal generators; presentation changes must never change mechanics or relabel pieces.
Record the seed and complete chronological legal witness with scramble provenance and an undo/recovery route.
Use a clearly labelled practice session unless the solver explicitly chooses another scope; do not overwrite personal solving work.
Apply active protection and fresh review requirements before deliberate execution; scrambling must not become automatic solving or a bypass of command gates.
A fixed 1,000-turn length is not a 1.0 contract.

rows.purpose: Choose which orbit state a subsequent operation must preserve.

Show every protected scope and check the complete operation at Net or Strict boundaries, including hidden labels and collateral.
Automatically protect only a transition from unfinished to exactly solved; new/reset sessions are not blanket locked and manual unlocks are not undone on unchanged state.
Invalidate execution permission after any state, workspace, protection, role, target or macro revision changes; recheck revisions, the full-state hash and protected objects before commit.

rows.purpose: Start from the exactly solved model while retaining a recovery point for displaced work.

requirements: Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Validate the reset scope before writes and publish solved labels plus a named recovery checkpoint transactionally.
Keep current preferences and the recovery checkpoint; distinguish resetting mechanics from resetting work presentation.
Invalidate pending execution permission and do not blanket-protect a new or reset session.
Failure must leave current work recoverable and must not be reported as a successful solve.

rows.purpose: Understand how work filters, references and motion detail affect inspection.

Distinguish full mechanics, interactive work and noninteractive references; show that camera detail and filters do not alter legal moves.
Define only the filter and projection facts the 1.0 UI uses, with short or cited proofs where correctness relies on them; replace legacy-only gesture guidance.

rows.purpose: Save a named fixed set of identities or positions for repeated work.

Capture exact matches and model identity in the session store, with an explicit identity-versus-position kind.
Keep a frozen set distinct from a live-query filter; show the current occupants of fixed positions and current locations of frozen identities.
Validate the full expression before publication and retain set membership across moves, view changes and resume without relabelling pieces.

rows.purpose: Name a destination for analysis while separating it from automatic insertion generation.

rows.purpose: Explicitly commit the complete operation whose current preview the solver has reviewed.

requirements: X-02: Keep checkpoint blob scans out of commit, undo and redo status refreshes; use lightweight metadata and check latency as automatic checkpoints accumulate.

rows.purpose: Choose a legal rotation around a focused cap and inspect its complete effect before execution.

Keep draft input and predicted state separate from committed state; rejected text must leave previous drafts and provenance intact.
Preview the full witness and collateral on all labelled slots, with current frame/protection evidence, then require explicit execution.
Use the shared notation and glossary with a keyboard route, without inheriting zero-based H/T captions as the 1.0 UX.

rows.purpose: Run actual MPUlt and Managed DirectX renderer/journal regressions through the retained host.
rows.reason: The mode exercises the runtime and bridge that charter section 4 replaces, so it serves only retained 0.4 infrastructure rather than a 1.0 flow.
rows.notes: Keep reusable fixture knowledge and matching-build evidence as source records. This proposal does not remove the 1.0 differential oracle, full-model correctness checks or actual Windows testing of the selected renderer, and claims no execution of the old mode.

rows.purpose: Measure camera, UI and scramble performance of the retained MPUlt/Managed DirectX host.
rows.reason: Charter sections 2 and 4 require evidence for the selected new renderer, and the briefing ends 0.4 performance work; this legacy benchmark mode cannot establish a 1.0 performance claim.
rows.notes: Reusable measurement methods and captured matching-build evidence remain inputs; this proposal omits the old benchmark command from 1.0. The new full-detail renderer gate and interaction measurements remain mandatory, with no native performance result claimed here.

rows.purpose: Collect a bounded local diagnostic record to help investigate a failure.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM and F-SESSION need traceable, recoverable failures; charter section 5 E6 and E7 and AGENTS.md's evidence boundary preserve diagnostics while replacing legacy directory scanning.
requirements: Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Collect only explicitly enumerated redacted diagnostic fields from the current build, with input/build identity and clear evidence status; old version-directory names must not determine coverage.
Bound collection work and artifact size, exclude databases, user puzzle data, tokens, credentials, geometry profiles and private paths, and preserve raw diagnostics locally.
Publish the requested local artifact atomically and make collection failure recoverable.
Collection never uploads or publishes data; external sharing requires its own owner authorization and review.

rows.purpose: Check the reflection-member surface of a supplied MPUlt PE/CLI assembly.
rows.reason: The required assembly types and members serve only the retained MPUlt host, which charter section 4 and section 5 anti-goal 1 exclude from 1.0.
rows.notes: Metadata inspection is not mathematical model verification, geometry certification or actual Windows/DirectX evidence. The surviving model/renderer identity purpose is recorded separately in U4-002.

rows.purpose: Apply a pinned text patch to an upstream MPUlt renderer checkout.
rows.reason: This optional source patch exists only for the retained renderer that charter section 4 replaces; no 1.0 solving or platform flow needs that purpose.
rows.notes: This is a feature-disposition proposal, not an instruction to edit or remove upstream source. Preserve Andrey Astrelin's primary MPUlt credit and upstream notices in retained source and evidence.

rows.purpose: Read local launch and diagnostic usage before invoking a tool.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM needs usable entry and diagnostics, and F-LEARN needs accurate guidance; charter section 5 E6 and E7 retain the purpose while the 0.4 command-line surfaces change.
requirements: Describe only supported 1.0 launch, session and local diagnostic operations with declared scope and prerequisites; remove help for legacy-only commands when their deletion is signed.
Help must be available before opening a database, starting an engine or modifying files, and must not trigger the operation it explains.
Keep wording reviewed and English, and distinguish source/fixture guidance from actual Windows or performance evidence.
rows.notes: All inventory entry points share the purpose of read-only usage guidance. The obsolete inspector/patcher flags are not a separate retained runtime contract, so this single-purpose unit is not split.

rows.purpose: Discover and reach the available commands from the current work context.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-LEARN need discoverability; charter section 4's single command table and section 5 E5 replace the old native menu organization.
requirements: Use one command ID and the same permission, busy and context gates for every key, pointer and menu invocation.
Expose every surviving command through the palette and a keyboard route, with engine-derived availability and an explanation when unavailable.
Use reviewed short labels and shared glossary terms, preserving command meanings across themes and soft key disclosure.
Do not copy the 0.4 menu groups or introduce a second invocation path around preview, protection or busy gates.
